walkthroughs.body_html:
Baptism initiates someone into the Church.

Infant baptism (Catholic, CofE, Methodist): babies are baptised; parents and godparents promise to raise them in faith.

Believer's baptism (Baptist, Pentecostal): only adults or older children who can confess faith — full immersion in water.

Matthew 28:19 — Jesus' Great Commission: 'go and make disciples. baptising them'.

At the Last Supper, Jesus said: 'This is my body. this is my blood' (Mark 14).

Christians celebrate this as the Eucharist (also Mass, Holy Communion, Lord's Supper).

Roman Catholics teach transubstantiation: bread and wine truly become Christ's body and blood. Anglicans see real spiritual presence. Methodists/Baptists often see it as memorial.

Christmas (25 December) celebrates the incarnation — Jesus' birth. Advent precedes it; carols, nativity plays and gift-giving mark the day.

Easter is the most important festival — Jesus' resurrection. Holy Week includes Maundy Thursday (Last Supper), Good Friday (crucifixion), and Easter Sunday (resurrection).

40 days later: Ascension. 10 days after that: Pentecost — the Spirit comes.

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
Christians believe in three different gods.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.

Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.
Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.

mcqs.q: Why do Jews not accept Jesus as the Messiah?
options: Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
Because Jews believe Jesus never existed.
Because the Jewish Messiah is expected to bring peace, rebuild the Temple and restore Israel — events the Jewish tradition holds Jesus did not accomplish.
Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.
